transcript.content: Hello, I'm Dr. Smith. It's nice to meet you. Could you tell me what brings you in to see me today?

Hi, Dr. Smith. It's really nice to meet you too. Thank you so much for taking the time to see me. 

Um... I guess the main reason I'm here is... well, I'm a registered nurse, and I've been having a little trouble at work. I'm sure everyone gets a bit scattered sometimes, right? But on the floor, I just keep losing my train of thought. Like, an IV pump will beep, or I'll hear someone ask another nurse a question, or a call light goes off, and... suddenly I've completely forgotten what patient flow issue I was working on. 

I mean, I always figure it out eventually, I don't want you to think I'm unsafe or doing a bad job! I really try my best. But it just happens constantly, and it's a little embarrassing. Am I explaining that okay? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right information.
Do you often feel like you have an internal motor that keeps you moving, or do you find it difficult to sit still for long periods, such as during meetings or while watching a movie?

Oh, um... no, I don't really get that feeling. I don't think I have an internal motor at all. I can sit through a movie or a staff meeting perfectly fine without needing to get up or move around. 

I mean, I might sort of... drift off in my head a little bit, but my body stays put! I actually really appreciate just sitting quietly when I get the chance, especially after being on my feet for a twelve-hour shift. 

I hope that's helpful? I know sometimes people assume you have to be really hyper and bouncing off the walls to have trouble focusing, but I'm actually pretty calm physically. I don't want to confuse things by not having that symptom. Did I answer that okay for you?
Do you find that you spend a significant amount of your time feeling worried or anxious about a wide range of different things, such as your job, your health, or your finances?

Um... no, I wouldn't say that. I mean, I think I worry a pretty normal amount? Like, everyone gets a little stressed about bills every now and then, right? But I definitely don't spend my whole day feeling anxious about a bunch of different things. 

Really, my main worry is just... well, work, like I mentioned, because I want to make sure I'm doing a good job for my patients and being a good teammate. But my health and finances and everything else are honestly fine. I'm generally a pretty positive person! 

I hope that makes sense? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right kind of information. Let me know if you need me to explain that better!
Over the past few weeks, have you found that you are no longer getting pleasure or enjoyment from the hobbies or activities that you usually love?

Oh, no, definitely not. I still really enjoy my hobbies. I mean, I love gardening and baking, and I still get a lot of joy out of doing those things on my days off. 

I guess sometimes I might... well, maybe I start a gardening project and kind of forget to finish it because I get distracted by something else in the yard, but the actual enjoyment is totally still there! I'm definitely not feeling down or depressed or anything like that. I still love the things I've always loved. 

Is that what you were looking for? I just want to be sure I'm answering your questions the right way so I'm not wasting your time.
Looking back at your childhood, did you have similar difficulties with staying focused or staying on task in school, even when you were young?

Um, well... yes, I suppose I did. I mean, I was always a really good kid, I promise! I wasn't disruptive or anything like that. But, um... yeah, even back in elementary school, my teachers would always write on my report cards that I was, you know, really bright, which was always nice of them to say! 

But they'd also usually add that I was... um, careless. Which always made me feel a little bad, because I really was trying my best. I just had a really hard time keeping track of things. I was always losing my worksheets, or I'd actually do my homework and then completely forget to turn it in. My mom actually had to sit with me every single night at the kitchen table just to keep me on track and make sure I finished everything. 

I feel a little embarrassed admitting that, because I really did want to be the perfect student and make my teachers happy. I hope that answers your question okay? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right kind of background history. Let me know if I'm talking too much!

Do you find that these difficulties with losing focus or forgetting to finish tasks also happen when you are at home or during your personal time, or is it strictly an issue you face while you are at work?

Um, well... I guess it's not just at work, no. I mean, I really try to keep things organized at home, I do! But... yeah, it happens there too. 

It's just silly little things, mostly. Like, um, things that should be totally routine? I might completely forget to call my mom back, or I'll realize I never followed up on a package that didn't arrive. Sometimes I'll even forget to pay a bill or... or show up for an appointment. 

Which sounds terrible, I know! I promise I don't do it on purpose. I always fully intend to do these things, and I even try setting reminders on my phone, but somehow... I just still manage to forget. It's really frustrating because I want to be reliable for my family and take care of my responsibilities. 

I hope I don't sound like a complete mess! I really am trying my best to stay on top of everything. Is that the kind of example you were looking for? I can try to explain it differently if that didn't make sense!
